messages:
priya (AcmeCorp): Hey — our desktop app embeds a WebView and we're seeing intermittent 500s from Redwood. Customers report no obvious request id in our logs. Any pointers for where to pull a request/trace id from an embedded WebView?

maya (Support): Thanks — we can definitely trace this if you can grab any of the following: X-Request-Id (response or request header), a debug token, or a HAR export showing the failing request. Quick checklist below.

priya (AcmeCorp): We can't open devtools in the shipped build. Is there a header name I should ask customers to look for?

maya (Support): Look for headers named `X-Request-Id` or `X-RW-Trace` (sometimes SDKs forward it as `x-request-id`). If you can intercept the network traffic, the header will be on the request/response. If header isn't present, a HAR or a curl repro works too.

eli (Eng): Practical capture options: 
- If you can remote-debug the WebView on Android: open `chrome://inspect` -> find the WebView -> right-click Inspect -> Network tab.
- For iOS: use Safari Develop -> <device> -> choose the WebView page -> Network.
- If you can't remote-debug, run a local proxy (mitmproxy/Charles/Fiddler) and capture the session. Export HAR from the proxy or browser devtools and attach.

maya (Support): Minimal curl repro we can use if you can run it from the same network (replace token):

```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: acme-desktop-12345" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

maya (Support): If you can include that `X-Request-Id` value in your logs we can correlate it to our server logs and pull the full trace. If you can't run curl, a HAR that contains the failing request is just as good.

priya (AcmeCorp): We can run the curl locally. If we don't see X-Request-Id in our client, will Redwood still log something?

eli (Eng): Yes — our backend will emit a server-side request id. But we need something to match on. If you can't provide a request id, give us: 
- exact UTC time window (start/end) of the failure,
- customer account id or org name,
- endpoint path (e.g., `/v1/generate`).
We can search logs by time/route and try to find the 500s.

maya (Support): If you can produce a debug token instead, include it as a query param `?debug_token=<token>` on a failing request or send it to us in the thread. Example (one-off, for trace retrieval):

```
https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?debug_token=debug_abc123
```

maya (Support): SDK tips: if you're using one of our client SDKs, enable verbose logging — it prints the request id on every call like `request_id=...`. Set env var `REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=debug` or enable the SDK's debug flag and re-run the failing flow. Attach the SDK logs (redact keys).

priya (AcmeCorp): Got it. We captured a HAR and ran the curl with `X-Request-Id: acme-desktop-12345`. Attached the HAR file and the curl output.

maya (Support): Perfect — thanks. We'll attach these to the escalation. @eli can you pull the server-side trace for `acme-desktop-12345` across 2026-03-17 15:20:00–15:30:00 UTC?

eli (Eng): On it. If I need a debug token I'll ask. For posterity: if customers are on tightly locked WebViews, the most reliable route is a proxy capture (mitmproxy/Charles) or adding a temporary debug build with remote devtools enabled.

dev-bot: Incident log created: INC-20260317-0023 — linked to this thread.

maya (Support): Quick summary checklist (copy/paste for support handoffs):
- Try to capture `X-Request-Id` (request or response header).
- If not available: HAR export or proxy capture.
- If possible: run curl with `X-Request-Id` header as minimal repro.
- Provide UTC time window + account/org name if no id.
- Attach SDK logs with debug enabled.

maya (Support): Thanks @priya — we'll follow up in this thread once we have the backend trace. :thumbsup:
